page: OVHcloud b2-120 is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 32 dedicated x86_64 physical cores powered by Intel Haswell architecture clocked at 2.0 GHz. The instance provides 120 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.75 GB of RAM per core. Hardware provisioning includes 400 GB of local SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps without bundled GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a clear dichotomy between single-threaded and parallel processing. Due to older architecture and modest clock speeds, single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, such as 947.88 on stress-ng and 1094 on Geekbench single-core tests. Conversely, the 32 dedicated physical cores deliver solid multi-core capacity, registering average tier performance across multi-threaded stress-ng (21855.61), Geekbench multi-core (7889.0), and PassMark CPU tests (29272.47).

Memory throughput and network throughput remain consistent with midrange demands, sustaining 92.99 GB/s large block read bandwidth and 38.32 GB/s write bandwidth. The server achieves 32.74 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.54 GB/s in static web serving throughput. Natural language generation speeds are constrained by single-thread limitations, though prompt ingestion matches median metrics.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the b2-120 prioritizes sheer core count and memory allocation over cutting-edge single-threaded capability. Workloads demanding high single-thread clock rates or vector instruction sets like AVX-512 will experience bottlenecks. Consequently, this server is suitable for horizontally scaled web services, multi-threaded batch operations, intermediate data processing, and multi-tenant hosting environments.
description: OVHcloud b2-120 is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by an Intel Haswell x86_64 processor delivering 32 dedicated physical cores at a 2.0 GHz base clock. The configuration pairs 120 GB of RAM (3.75 GB per core) with 400 GB of local SSD storage and a 10 Gbps baseline network interface, without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate modest single-thread metrics, landing in lower evaluation tiers across stress-ng and Geekbench. However, its 32 physical execution cores achieve solid mid-tier multi-threaded throughput, evidenced by 21,855.61 on stress-ng multi-core and 29,272.47 on PassMark CPU tests. Memory subsystem bandwidth reaches 92.99 GB/s for large uncached reads, effectively supporting Redis workloads at 32.74 million operations per second. While single-thread limitations hinder latency-sensitive tasks and rapid LLM text generation, the instance offers strong resource density for parallel tasks, batch processing, static web serving, and distributed database services.
